title: copper-ridge-payments-integration-call-notes-2026-07-15
content:
Call with Copper Ridge Payments (CRP) - 2026-07-15 
Attendees: Asha Patel (Redwood, SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood, Solutions Eng), Maya Thompson (Redwood, PM), Liam O'Connor (CRP, Eng Lead), Priya Singh (CRP, Product), Evan Moore (CRP, Security)

TL;DR
- CRP evaluating Redwood for transaction classification + fraud signal enrichment. Interested in hosted API for PoC, Dedicated for production (SLA + throughput), and Private for regulatory needs later.
- Primary concerns: PII handling, latency (p99 < 200ms for classification path), cost per transaction, and model explainability / audit logs.
- Next step: share tailored PoC plan + sample prompt set and lightweight SDK integration guide by 2026-07-18.

Integration scope (from call notes)
- Use case: real-time classification of payment metadata + short issuer notes (<= 256 chars) to return: category, fraud-risk-score (0-100), reasons (3 bullet points).
- Avg TPS expected during PoC: 10 tps, peak burst to 50 tps. Production target: sustained 500 tps with spikes to 2k tps (for Dedicated sizing).
- Max acceptable latency for end-to-end classification (Redwood call + app processing) p99: 200ms. Target p50 < 40ms.

Data & Security
- Data contains card-present metadata, card network tokens, but CRP will strip full PANs prior to sending. Still PII-ish -> they need SOC2 + HIPAA posture docs (they are in payments, some healthcare customers).
- KMS requirement for any Private deployment; key rotation policy needed. For Hosted: they want host-managed KMS + option to bring-your-own-key for Dedicated/Private.
- Logging/audit: they need request/response hashes stored for 90 days; full payload retention needs governance - propose redact/store only metadata + deterministic hash.

Auth & Rate limiting
- API keys for PoC; for production CRP wants mTLS or token binding for Dedicated. Rate limit / quota enforcement per integration key + per-route. Need sample policy.

Model/Quality expectations
- They prefer an open model baseline (cost reasons) with Redwood-verified performance. Interested in a compact quantized model for latency (e.g., 7B family) but want fallback to higher-quality model for ambiguous cases (A/B or canary).
- Explainability: require structured reasons field (3 bullets) and confidence score mapping. We may use function-calling/structured output to enforce schema.

Throughput & infra notes (internal)
- For PoC: host on Redwood API with presized concurrent requests and KV prefix caching for repeated merchant patterns. Batching is NOT acceptable for real-time path unless latency remains within SLO. Consider micro-batching with 10ms windows for cost tests only.
- For Dedicated sizing: estimate for 500 tps sustained (classification only, small outputs ~ 50 tokens): likely need multiple GPU workers with autoscaling headroom. Flag to infra for capacity planning.

Integration gotchas / open questions (to resolve)
- Q1: Do they need deterministic responses for audit? If yes, we should pin model versions and disable non-deterministic sampling.
- Q2: What is their retention policy for logs beyond 90 days? Who owns deletion workflow?
- Q3: If they want Private on-prem, networking (VPC peering vs on-prem appliance) decision will drive timeline. Need network topology details.
- Q4: How will they route fallback: higher-quality model vs different region? Clarify policy.

Action items (owners & ETA)
- A1: Draft PoC plan with integration PR template + SDK snippet (Python + Node) - owner: Asha - due 2026-07-18.
- A2: Security checklist (KMS options, retention controls, SOC2 artifacts) + short presales packet - owner: Diego - due 2026-07-19.
- A3: Engineering sizing draft for Dedicated (capacity + cost ballpark) - owner: Diego + infra - due 2026-07-22.
- A4: Request sample redacted payloads from CRP (5-10 examples) for prompt/quality tuning - owner: Liam (CRP) - target 2026-07-17.
- A5: Schedule follow-up deep-dive on latency & routing (include infra + SRE) - owner: Maya - target meeting week of 2026-07-20.

Notes to self (informal)
- Priya emphasized that explainability & auditability will be an immediate blocker for procurement; prepare example outputs with structured reasons and a short human-readable explanation template.
- Watch out: CRP wants to compare unit economics vs their current rule engine. Need to prepare per-transaction cost comparison (including caching/batching savings).
- Keep PoC minimal: classification single-response path, no streaming, no long context. Avoid introducing embeddings for now unless they ask for offline retraining/nearest-neighbor.

Follow-ups completed/changes
- Sent calendar invite for follow-up deep dive (Maya) - added CRP SRE + our infra.
- Uploaded initial SDK snippets to GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cust-integ-templates/pull/42 (wip).

Unresolved / decision log (put into confluence if agreed)
- Need decision on model determinism vs stochastic for production. If they require deterministic, add to contract and pin model versions.

End notes
- This feels like a strong mid-market opportunity (payments vertical) - prioritize around Dedicated + optional Private down the line. Keep touchpoints short and technical.

-- Asha
